data.narrative:
Kairos Power is a late-stage nuclear energy company that has raised $500M+ to date. The valuation universe for advanced nuclear comprises 3 public comparables (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 5 private peers including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and TerraPower. The sector remains nascent with limited late-stage nuclei, constraining traditional peer multiples.

Given data constraints, only the Stage-Progression method is applicable. This approach applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier to the $500M total raised proxy, reflecting typical valuation progression from late-stage private to pre-exit positioning, yielding $600M. A Peer-Median approach was not viable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow nuclear energy cohort; fewer than three datapoints met filtering criteria. Peer data exists but remains too dispersed across valuation tiers and development stages to anchor a robust median.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $510M to $690M, with a median estimate of $600M. This range reflects upside from the $500M raised (low end) and reasonable step-up progression (median), with the high end accommodating later-round momentum. Material uncertainties include regulatory approval timelines, technology validation progress relative to competing modular reactor designs, and absence of disclosed financials or unit economics. A second triangulation method grounded in comparable transactions or revenue multiples would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
